newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iraq's Saddam must leave power - Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Saddam must leave power - Kuwait.

text.p: Kuwait said on Saturday the Gulf region would never be secure until Iraqi President Saddam Hussein left power but stressed that it was not advocating Saddam's overthrow.

"The crisis will never be over untill Saddam Hussein goes," Information Minister Sheikh Saud Nasser al-Saud al-Sabah told a news conference. "We would like to see, once and for all, an end to this regime sooner rather than later."
Asked if he was directly advocating Saddam's overthrow, he replied: "I am not advocating anything."
The minister said there was an international consensus that Saddam was a threat to the region.

U.S. Secretary of Defence William Perry is due to arrive in Kuwait on Sunday to discuss growing tension between Baghdad and Washington and "further measures" to deal with the current crisis, Sheikh Saud added.
With most regional allies unwilling to take part in the current U.S. military buildup, Washington is despatching added warships to the region and 5,000 troops to Kuwait.
Eight Stealth radar-evading bombers landed in Kuwait on Friday as part of preparations for a possible military strike against Iraq.
